full_judgment: 4. Defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that there was no cause of action for filing the suit and the suit as framed was not maintainable and the suit was barred by limitation and that civil Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit since the subject matter of the suit was the subject matter of the Administrative Tribunal. The definite case of defendant No.3 was that he joined the Madrasha on August 1, 1964 and in 1969 he was promoted as Mohaddes and when the post of Principal of the Madrasha had fallen vacant, the Madrasha Managing Committee advertised for filling up the post of Principal. He applied and was appointed Principal by the Managing Committee. The plaintiff applied for the post of Vice Principal but he was not selected. There was an audit of the accounts of the Madrasha by the Office of the Auditor and Accountant General and in the audit report the plaintiff was shown as an additional teacher. The plaintiff was directed to return the amount drawn by him as Head Mohaddes. The plaintiff was found surplus teacher. The Managing Committee released him from service as per rules of the Madrasha Board and the release of the plaintiff was quite legal.
